title: Athenian Coalition
capsule: The Athenian Coalition was the alliance of Greek poleis led by Athens and Aetolia formed immediately after Alexander the Great's death in June 323 BCE to resist Macedonian supremacy — the conflict known as the Lamian War. Under the general Leosthenes, the coalition trapped the regent Antipater in Lamia through the winter of 323/322 BCE, but Leosthenes was killed in the siege; Macedonian-Thessalian relief forces under Craterus crushed the Greek army at Crannon in August 322 BCE and destroyed the allied fleet at Amorgos. The defeat ended Athenian democratic self-government: Antipater imposed a property-franchise oligarchy and Demosthenes died in flight. The dataset's terminal date of –256 may extend the entity to encompass the later Chremonidean War (268–261 BCE), when Athens again organized coalition resistance before final Macedonian occupation.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The political and military narrative is well attested in Diodorus Siculus and Plutarch; territorial control is poorly bounded and largely coextensive with the participating polis hinterlands rather than a unified administered state.
